en.note:
The idea

Dutch spelling is very regular, but it has a few marks that English uses differently or not at all: the apostrophe in plurals, the diaeresis (ë, ï), the hyphen in compound words. And some capitalization rules work the opposite way from English. Here are the rules you really need to write a text or an email without mistakes.

The apostrophe: plurals

After a word ending in a long vowel a, i, o, u, y, the -s plural takes an apostrophe so the vowel stays long: auto's, foto's, menu's, pagina's, baby's. In English an apostrophe in a plural is a mistake; in Dutch it's the rule here. After -é and after a silent -e there's no apostrophe: cafés, tantes (tante = aunt).

The apostrophe: the possessive

With people's names you can say de fiets van Anna or add -s:

the name ends in…form
a consonant or silent -eJans fiets, Annes fiets (no apostrophe)
a long vowel a, i, o, u, yAnna's fiets, Marco's fiets
-s, -x, -zThomas' fiets (apostrophe only)

Careful: Jan's fiets is a mistake copied from English. Also note 's avonds (in the evening), 's morgens (in the morning): here 's is an old article and is always lowercase.

The diaeresis (het trema)

When two vowels next to each other could be read as one sound, the diaeresis shows that a new syllable starts (as in English "naïve"): België, Italië, ideeën, zeeën, ruïne, tweeëntwintig, drieëntwintig.

The hyphen (het koppelteken)

In compound words, if the first part ends in a vowel and the second starts with a vowel that could merge with it, use a hyphen (not the diaeresis): zee-egel, auto-ongeluk, zonne-energie, na-apen. The hyphen is also used in compound place names: West-Vlaanderen, Oost-Vlaanderen, Sint-Niklaas.

Capital letters

Unlike German, common nouns are lowercase. Unlike English, days and months are lowercase: maandag, dinsdag, mei. As in English, languages and nationality adjectives are capitalized: Nederlands, Italiaans, een Italiaanse auto. Unlike English "I", ik is lowercase. The letter ij at the start of a proper name becomes IJ: de IJzer (the Yser river), IJsland.

Commas and quotation marks

If the subordinate clause comes before the main clause, you usually put a comma between the two verbs: Omdat het regent, blijf ik thuis. If it comes after, the comma is optional. Direct speech is introduced with a colon (not a comma as in English) and starts with a capital: Hij zegt: "Ik kom morgen."

Watch out: typical mistakes for English speakers

  • Capitalizing months and days as in English: in Mei → in mei, op Maandag → op maandag.
  • English-style possessive apostrophe: Jan's boek → Jans boek.
  • Plural without the apostrophe: fotos → foto's.
  • Capitalizing ik like "I": Morgen kom Ik → Morgen kom ik.
  • Forgetting the diaeresis: Belgie → België.
en.vlaams: The spelling rules are the same in Belgium and the Netherlands: they're set by the Nederlandse Taalunie (Dutch Language Union) and summed up in the "Groene Boekje" (Green Booklet). Belgian provinces are written with a hyphen: West-Vlaanderen, Oost-Vlaanderen, Vlaams-Brabant.

hard.q: Which of these sentences has no spelling mistakes?
o: Op dinsdag rijden we met Anna's auto naar West-Vlaanderen.
Op Dinsdag rijden we met Anna's auto naar West-Vlaanderen.
Op dinsdag rijden we met Annas auto naar West-Vlaanderen.
Op dinsdag rijden we met Anna's auto naar West Vlaanderen.
hard.e: Three rules at once: days lowercase (dinsdag, unlike English), an apostrophe after a long vowel (Anna's), a hyphen in compound place names (West-Vlaanderen).

g.Op dinsdag rijden we met Anna's auto naa: On Tuesday we're driving to West Flanders in Anna's car (correct)
g.Op dinsdag rijden we met Annas auto naar: after a long vowel you need the apostrophe: Anna's
g.Op dinsdag rijden we met Anna's auto naa: compound province names need a hyphen

hard.tt: On Tuesday we're driving to West Flanders in Anna's car.

hard.e: drie + en + tachtig: the vowels e-e collide, so a diaeresis: drieëntachtig, all one word.

hard.e: 's avonds: 's stays lowercase even at the start of a sentence (the capital goes on the next word: 's Avonds). The language is capitalized: Italiaans. After 's avonds in first position: inversion.
